patch.description: Assigning an `open` or `reopened` complaint starts work (`in_progress`). Manual moves: `open`/`reopened` -> `in_progress`; `in_progress` -> `resolved` (note required); `open`/`in_progress` -> `closed` (reason required, for duplicates or mistakes). Engineering cannot close a `resolved` complaint: the unit does, by acknowledging the returned device or with `confirm`. Every change writes a system comment.
patch.summary: Assign, prioritise or move a complaint (admin, engineer)

post.description: `resolved` -> `closed`. Returns 409 `AWAITS_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` when a returned device must be acknowledged instead.

post.description: `resolved` -> `reopened`, with a required reason. Returns 409 `AWAITS_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` when a returned device must be disputed instead.

patch.description: Only `device_type`, `serial_number`, `make`, `model` and `acquired_on`. Status and unit are rejected (422): they change only through events. Every real change writes a `note_added` event describing it; a patch that changes nothing writes nothing.

post.description: Moves the device through its life cycle. Each `event_type` takes exactly its own fields; unknown fields are rejected and the server stamps the time. An event that does not fit the device's current status returns `409 INVALID_TRANSITION` listing the allowed events. The device row is locked, so two simultaneous events cannot both succeed from the same state. `assigned_to_unit`, `received_for_repair` and `returned_to_unit` must then be acknowledged by the unit. `returned_to_unit` and the steps between intake and return are linked to the repair's ticket automatically.

get.description: Events in chronological order with actor, counterparty, diagnosis, linked ticket and acknowledgement state (`not_required`, `pending`, `confirmed`, `disputed`; pending events report `pending_days` and `overdue`). `date_from` / `date_to` are inclusive calendar days in Africa/Lagos.

Newest first. A unit rep sees only events of devices in their own unit; a `unit_id` filter from a unit rep is ignored. For staff, `unit_id` matches the unit recorded on the event. `date_from` / `date_to` are inclusive Africa/Lagos days.

post.description: Only for `assigned_to_unit`, `received_for_repair` and `returned_to_unit`, once per event. A dispute needs a comment and never changes history: engineering answers with a `note_added` event. Disputing a returned device reopens its ticket; confirming it closes the ticket. Another unit's event returns 403; an acknowledged one returns 409.
post.summary: Confirm or dispute an event (unit rep of that unit)
